features: WHAT VANISHED WITHOUT SAYING SO — The dashboard said the instalment plan needed recalculating. You pressed «Recalculate», the dialog answered «Operation Completed», and nothing changed: you could press it forever. The measured case: a plan with € 35,661.60 of budget items generated € 2,400.00, and the remaining € 33,261.60 went nowhere — not into an instalment, not into a warning, not into an error. No migration, and no data changes on its own.

WHY THEY VANISHED. The software already knows what to do when an expense cannot be allocated: it declares it uncovered, stops the generation and asks for a written justification. That guard, however, lived in a part of the engine that instalment plans never go through, because a plan always forces the amount of its budget items and takes a different route. The protection existed, was covered by tests, and for instalment plans it never once fired.

THREE POINTS, NOT ONE. Three places turned out to let money out silently: a budget item with no thousandths table linked (the reported case); a table that is linked but empty, with no units assigned or every thousandth at zero; and the same case with several tables, which is worse — there the amount did not vanish, it was redistributed onto the participants of the other tables. People who had nothing to do with it paid. All three now stop and ask what to do.

THE SCREEN SAYS WHAT IS MISSING AND WHERE TO FIX IT. The uncovered-amounts panel could tell one story only — «this unit has nobody to charge» — because until yesterday that was the only possible case. It now tells three, each with its remedy: «No thousandths table linked to this budget item», «Table X has no usable thousandths — assign the units and enter the values», «Flat 3 — register the missing owners». It behaves identically when creating a plan and when recalculating one.

Fixed — THE AMOUNTS WERE DIVIDED BY A HUNDRED: in that same dialog, an uncovered amount of € 24,741.60 appeared as € 247.42. At the very point where you are asked to accept an unallocated expense in writing, the figure was a hundredth of the real one. The defect predates this version and was rarely seen, precisely because that dialog almost never opened.

Fixed — «OPERATION COMPLETED» NO LONGER APPEARS WHEN IT ISN'T. With the engine fixed, the message kept lying: the green dialog opened on top of the panel listing what was missing. It happened because a rejected operation goes back, and going back is, to the program, a successful response.

THE THOUSANDTHS TOTAL, AS YOU TYPE IT. Assigning thousandths to units, there was no total at all: you filled it in row by row and noticed a typo at the first allocation, or never — because the engine always distributes 100% of the expense over the effective total, so a table missing a unit makes the others pay that share with nothing to flag it. There is now a sum at the foot of the table, moving as you type. It passes no judgement and does not demand 1000: on real tables 1000 is often not the right number — partial ones, equal-share ones, ones rounded by the surveyor and approved that way by the assembly.

THOUSANDTHS ARE WRITTEN WITH THE TABLE'S OWN DECIMALS. Values now appear with the declared number of decimals — 500.00, not 500.00000 — and beyond those decimals you cannot type: on a two-decimal table, the third digit does not go in. Also fixed an inconsistent limit: 5 decimals on creation and 6 on editing, against a column that stores 5, with the sixth silently truncated.

SOMEONE ELSE'S DEBT CAN NO LONGER BE PAID BY MISTAKE. When searching payments by property unit, the screen gathers the shares of all co-owners under the same row: the debt may belong to one person while another is paying. Allocating there, the software said yes and did nothing — with credit it withdrew it and handed it straight back, with cash it turned it into an advance for the payer, leaving open the very debt you meant to settle. It now stops and says whose debt that is.

Fixed — THE «MISALIGNED» BADGE THAT WOULD NOT GO OUT. On a management with a joint debt — the kind that follows the unit rather than the person — the instalment plan panel stayed red even on a perfectly correct plan, and no recalculation could turn it off. Same symptom as the original report, from a second cause. Fixing it revealed that the dashboard panel and the plan page answered «is this plan aligned?» with two different methods and two different tolerances: a plan one euro out was green on one and urgent on the other. There is now a single answer.

Under the bonnet: thirty-four new tests, fifteen of them on the frontend, including the first test files for two components that had none. The badge fix deleted the one written the day before — reading the expense component directly makes subtracting the balances unnecessary, and is immune to the joint-debt problem by construction. A critical code review, run before release, found three defects in what this version had just written, including a new guard that would have reached the administrator as an error page, throwing away the allocation they had just entered by hand.
